messages.subject: Re: Struggling to initialize model: Node inconsistent with parents
parts:
In general, the "inconsistent with parents" message means that there is some sort of impossible incompatibility among the values specified by the data/model/initial values for the indicated object, so perhaps scrutiny of the places where you define D will reveal some inconsistency.

I'm wondering if it has something to do with this line:
D[j] ~ dbin(zp[j], N[j])  

Any chance that N is not large enough to allow values of D up to 21 or 27, given the mean of zp?

Hope that might give you a place to start, anyway!

Emily

On Fri, Jun 7, 2019 at 1:09 PM Ali Yost <ayo...@sdsu.edu> wrote:
Hi all,
I am very new to JAGs and modeling in general and I am having issues initializing a multi-species hierarchical model modified from Rich et al. (2017) (model I am using created by Dr. Chen at National Chung Hsing University). I am getting an error that seems to be common issue for new modelers: Error in jags.model(model.file, data = data, inits = init.values, n.chains = n.chains,  :  Error in node D[3]    Node inconsistent with parents

When I look at D[3] (third detection value listed) I see that it is 21. If I set it to 0 or 1, the error moves on to the next node, a value of 27. In fact, through trial and error I found if I set all detection values greater than 7 to equal 1 instead of their true values, the model runs, however, I do not understand why. Perhaps a fluke, but the error seems to point to the same 45 nodes every time. This code works unaltered with a larger dataset with maximum number of detections of 19 while the highest number of detections in my dataset is 71. In addition, I have zero observations for one of 19 species studied. 

I would greatly appreciate any suggestion to help me through this issue and understanding why it occurred! Resources like these have been essential for self-teaching and I appreciate respondents for taking the time to share their knowledge. I apologize if this is a simple question and any naiveté on my end. 

Best,
Ali Yost

M.S.GIS Graduate Student
Department of Geography
San Diego State University
ayo...@sdsu.edu


CODE:

#Load data
Data_human = read.csv("Data_human_Yost.csv", header = TRUE)
#read species list
Spp<-read.csv (file=paste ("Species.csv", sep=""))
# Next load several packages:
library(R2jags); library(reshape2); library(plyr);library(reshape2)
#When prompted for GCRAN mirror site, you may choose USA (CA1)[https] and click on OK.
#Define the group variables 
G <-cbind(as.numeric(Data_human $Size=="Mammal-Small"),as.numeric(Data_human$Size=="Mammal-Medium"),as.numeric(Data_human$Size=="Mammal-Large"))
#Define the covariates for occupancy 
X = Data_human[,c(7:12)] 
#Define the group covariates 
XG = cbind(X*G[,1],X*G[,2],X*G[,3]) 
#Define the covariates for detection 
dX = Data_human[13]
#Load the necessary libraries 


#Define the necessary arguments to run the jags command 
#Load all the data including the detection array, number of sampling occasions, individual 
#species sampled, total number of sampled species, and covariate information  

#Data_human$detections[Data_human$detections>10]=1
#Data_human$detections[]=1
#Data_human$detections[]=1


data <- list(D = Data_human$detections, N = ceiling(Data_human[,"num.survey"]), Species =  
               as.numeric(Data_human$SppCode), n = nrow(Data_human), nspp = 
               max(as.numeric(Data_human$SppCode)),X = X, XG = XG, dX = dX) 
#Specify the initial values...to be values greater than 0 so that JAGS doesn't initialize
#the occupancy status of that location to 0 (no occupancy)
inits = function() {list(Z = as.numeric(data$D>0))}

#Specify the parameters to be monitored 
params = c("rho","pbeta","spbeta","sigpbeta","mbeta","sigbeta","sbeta","gbeta",  
           "psi.mean","sigma.occ","p.mean","sigma.p","alpha","Z","P")
#Specify the number of chains (nc), number of iterations (ni), burn-in period (nb), and thinning 
#rate (nthin) 
nc = 3 
ni = 60000 
nb = 10000
nthin = 50
i=1


#Write the model code to a text file called "AllMammals.txt" 
cat(" 
    
    data { 
    nBeta <- dim(X) 
    nG <- dim(XG) 
    nP <- dim(dX) 
    } 
    
    model { 
    
    # Define covariance parameter between detection and mean occupancy  
    rho ~ dunif(-1,1) 
    var.p <- sigma.p /(1.-pow(rho,2)) 
    
    #Define prior distributions for occupancy parameters 
    alpha.mean <- log(psi.mean) - log(1-psi.mean) 
    psi.mean ~ dunif(0,1) 
    sigma.occ ~ dunif(0,10) 
    tau.occ <- pow(sigma.occ,-2) 
    
    #Define prior distributions for true positive detections 
    p.mean ~ dunif(0,1) 
    b <- log(p.mean) - log(1-p.mean) 
    sigma.p ~ dunif(0,10) 
    tau.p <- pow(sigma.p,-2) 
    
    #Define prior distributions for occupancy effects where nbeta is the number of occupancy 
    #covariates in the model, mbeta is the community-level hyper-parameter for each of the nbeta 
    #covariates, tbeta is the amount of variability in each of the community-level hyper-parameters, 
    #and sbeta is the species-specific covariate effects 
    for (a in 1:nBeta[2]){ 
    mbeta[a] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)   
    sigbeta[a] ~ dunif(0,10) 
    tbeta[a] <- pow(sigbeta[a],-2)   
    for (i in 1:(nspp)) {     
    sbeta[i,a] ~ dnorm(0,tbeta[a])   
    } 
    } 
    
    #Define prior distributions for nG, the group-level hyper-parameters 
    for (a in 1:nG[2]){ 
    gbeta[a] ~ dnorm(0,0.01) 
    } 
    
    #Define prior distributions for detection effects where nP is the number of detection covariates in 
    #the model, pbeta is the community-level hyper-parameter for each of the nP covariates, tpbeta is 
    #the amount of variability in each of the community-level hyper-parameters, and spbeta is the 
    #species-specific covariate effects 
    for (a in 1:nP[2]){ 
    pbeta[a] ~ dnorm(0,0.01) 
    sigpbeta[a] ~ dunif(0,10) 
    tpbeta[a] <- pow(sigpbeta[a],-2)   
    for (i in 1:(nspp)) {     
    spbeta[i,a] ~ dnorm(0,tpbeta[a])   
    } 
    } 
    
    #Define prior distributions for the occupancy and detection covariates for each species  
    for (i in 1:(nspp)) { 
    alpha[i] ~ dnorm(alpha.mean, tau.occ) 
    mu.p[i] <- b + (rho*sigma.p /sigma.occ)*(alpha[i] - alpha.mean) 
    P[i] ~ dnorm(mu.p[i], var.p) 
    } 
    
    #Estimate the occupancy probability (latent Z matrix) for each species at each camera station 
    for (j in 1:n) { 
    logit(psi[j]) <- alpha[Species[j]] + inprod(mbeta,X[j,])+ inprod(sbeta[Species[j],],  
    X[j,]) + inprod(gbeta,XG[j,]) 
    
    #Estimate the detection probability for each species at each camera station 
    logit(p[j]) <- P[Species[j]] + inprod(pbeta,dX[j,]) + inprod(spbeta[Species[j],],  
    dX[j,])     
    
    Z[j] ~ dbern(psi[j]) 
    zp[j] <- p[j]*Z[j] 
    D[j] ~ dbin(zp[j], N[j]) 
    } 
    } 
    
    #Finish writing the text file 
    ", file = "AllMammals.txt") 

#Run the model and call the results "output" 
output<- jags(data = data, inits = inits, parameters.to.save = params, model.file  
              ="AllMammals.txt", n.chains =nc, n.iter =ni, n.burnin =nb, n.thin =nthin)
